findings.title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from 'recreate needed' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body:
`RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` moves from 4 to 3, and the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` takes over 4. Any script or pipeline written against the previous behavior treats exit 4 as "rolling upgrade not possible, do a recreate". After this change, those scripts will:

- read a missing-feature configuration error (4) as a legitimate recreate decision;
- not recognise the new recreate code (3).

Reusing a code with a different meaning silently breaks existing consumers instead of failing loudly. Either use a previously unused code for `FEATURE_DISABLED` or clearly call out the exit-code change in the release/migration notes.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test checks neither exit code nor the `check` subcommand
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only runs the `metadata` subcommand and only asserts the error message. It never verifies that the process exits with the documented `FEATURE_DISABLED` code (4). It also never exercises the identical guard added to `UpdateCompatibilityCheck`. A regression in the exit code (the very contract the docs tell scripts to rely on) or in the `check` guard would go unnoticed.
